\begin{figure}[h]
  \captionsetup{font=footnotesize}
  \caption{\textbf{Multi-timescale structure of behavior in a virtual patch-foraging task.}
    (\subref{fig:1-a}) (Left) Head-fixed mice ran on a wheel through a multi-sensory virtual odor patch foraging environment. (Right) High, low, and unrewarded patch types were cued by different odors (orange, green, or purple). Patch types differed in initial reward probability (a), and depleted with each reward collected.
    (\subref{fig:1-b}) Running velocity (black trace), stop choice tones (red dots), rewards (blue dots), and odor sites for example patches in a session.
    (\subref{fig:1-c}) Running velocity revealed stereotyped stop actions at odor site entries and longer stop times in rewarded vs unrewarded sites.
    (\subref{fig:1-d}) Mice foraged in two rewarded patch types, stopping more in the high value type, and (\subref{fig:1-e}) consistently skipping the unrewarded patch type (across mice, n=24)
    (\subref{fig:1-f}-\subref{fig:1-t}) Behavior was organized across nested timescales: sites (sub-second), patches (tens of seconds to minutes), and sessions (tens of minutes).
    (\subref{fig:1-g}-\subref{fig:1-k})  Stereotyped action motifs at the odor site level. Velocity and sniffing in an odor site shaded by HMM states (\subref{fig:1-g}) and as trajectory in velocity and sniff frequency state space (\subref{fig:1-h}).
    (\subref{fig:1-i}--\subref{fig:1-k}) HMM states (one row per site; same session as in \subref{fig:1-b}) and mean velocity aligned to the minimum intersite distance (\subref{fig:1-i}), site entry (\subref{fig:1-j}) and average reward delay time (\subref{fig:1-k}) (grey-animal average, black-grand mean; n=13 mice).
      (\subref{fig:1-m}-\subref{fig:1-p}) Action motifs changed as mice approached patch leaving decision. HMM states (\subref{fig:1-m}) and velocity-sniff trajectories  (\subref{fig:1-n}) colored by sites from patch leaving.
    (\subref{fig:1-o}) Mice entered odor sites with decreased sniff frequency, increased velocity, and (\subref{fig:1-p}) had slower reaction times later in the patch  (mean $\pm$ s.e.m., $n=13$ mice).
    (\subref{fig:1-r},\subref{fig:1-t}) Session-averaged probability of three engagement states (engaged, disengage-run, disengage-stop; mean $\pm$ s.e.m. across sessions) for two mice, one disengaged by stopping (\subref{fig:1-r}, $n=20$ sessions) the other disengaged by running (\subref{fig:1-t}, $n=18$ sessions).
    (\subref{fig:1-s}) Velocity and sniff frequency reflect engagement across an early (left) and late (right) period of an example session.}
  \label{fig:1}
\end{figure}
